adviser_answers.question: what must a telehealth provider do before sharing patient information with another facility
adviser_answers.ruling: the text says that before sharing patient information with another facility or entity, a telehealth provider must obtain the patient's explicit consent. The transfer of information must be limited to the needs required by the patient's health condition. Additionally, providers must adopt accurate procedures on how to transfer, save, store, protect, and maintain the confidentiality of the patient's data. If an alternative service provider is recommended, the physician must ensure all necessary patient information and data is transferred through patient consent. (Note added by the system: the cited documents are guidance, standards or summaries, not binding law.)

The DHA Standards for Telehealth Services are Version 4, issued in 2025 and effective as of 2025-11-26, representing the current standard but subject to future updates.
The patient's consent must be explicit and obtained prior to the transfer of information.
The scope of the information shared must be strictly limited to what is necessary for the patient's health condition.

adviser_answers.question: Abu Dhabi health information exchange rules for sharing patient data between facilities
adviser_answers.ruling: the text says that healthcare facilities are generally required to obtain patient consent before sharing patient data via the ADHIE platform, though the DOH requires and authorizes the sharing and receiving of such data without consent for legacy data or under specific instructions in accordance with applicable laws. All systems and processes involved in the exchange must comply with the Abu Dhabi Health Information and Cyber Security Standard (ADHICS) and other relevant information security regulations. The policy aims to maximize the number of patients whose data is available through the ADHIE platform by encouraging universal participation and adherence to platform access requirements and interface standards. (Note added by the system: the cited documents are guidance, standards or summaries, not binding law.)
conditions: The policy is effective as of April 16, 2020, but it is not confirmed whether it has been replaced or superseded by a newer version.
Healthcare facilities must obtain patient consent for sharing data unless the DOH specifically authorizes sharing without consent (e.g., for legacy data) under applicable laws and instructions.
All data exchange and systems must comply with the ADHICS and other relevant information security regulations, as well as platform access and interface standards.

adviser_answers.question: Dubai health information sharing policy for patient data between health entities
adviser_answers.ruling: the text says that any sharing of protected health information between entities in Dubai must be based on patient consent or another legal condition. It also requires that within an entity, access to PHI be limited to staff with a legitimate professional reason. When care is transferred, a copy of the medical record may be sent directly or via request, but separate patient consent is required. Systematic sharing of the same data sets between the same entities is permitted only in accordance with applicable legislation and without written consent except in legally specified cases. (Note added by the system: the cited documents are guidance, standards or summaries, not binding law.)
